L2 oracle: the grammar's own queries/tags.scm and locals.scm (tree-sitter/tree-sitter-ruby v0.23.1, MIT) run by py-tree-sitter 0.25.2 with tree-sitter-ruby 0.23.1, tier C (D5, calibration/oracles/ts-tags), so L2 is capped at good; the script's tag set equals `tree-sitter tags` 0.26.11's on both subjects (20,073 and 16,825 tags). Its pairs count every constant and every non-local identifier as a call: the dialect takes the method name of each call node and every constant, so its 1,110 missed pairs (of 8,463) are bare identifiers with no receiver (`params`, `settings`, a reader called in its own class), which a syntactic query cannot tell from a local variable read, and its 46 pairs outside the oracle are `super`, which upstream's pattern does not tag. call_recall was .6622 before constants became call targets (and the same dialect held sym_recall .9451, L1 good, before constants, attr_* names, aliases and define_method became definitions).

Ruby names a constant lexically, so a reference to Base inside module Sinatra reaches Sinatra::Base, which the resolver's bare top-level match cannot see: only a class, module or constant defined at the top of its file, or a top-level method, resolves; a nested definition does not. Edges keep the file-resolved label, tier pre-scan.

changes to the previous ruby dialect (same SourceKinds kept, every symbol it listed still emitted, TestRubyDialectKeepsLegacySymbols): new are RubyConstant (a container, so `Outer::CONST` and the methods of a Struct.new block qualify), RubyProperty (attr_accessor, attr_reader and attr_writer names, qualified `Owner.name`), RubyAlias (`alias` and `alias_method`), RubyMethod for define_method with a literal name, RubyClass and RubyModule for `Name = Class.new` and `Module.new` (and bound to a local), a constant reference as a call target, and .rake, .ru and Rakefile as Ruby. Not emitted, on purpose: a bare identifier as a call, `def obj.x` on a local (no owner to qualify it), `attr :x`, and the assignments ctags does not read either (`A, B = 1, 2`, `X ||= 1`, `A::B = 1`).

file_edge_precision and file_edge_recall measured against an import dump's (file, imported file) pairs, there being no SCIP index: the truth is what each file's import statements name, not the files its references reach as a SCIP index's cross-file edges are, so a file reached without an import of its own (a file another one required, an autoloaded constant) is outside the truth and a resolved edge to it counts against precision, while a file imported and never referenced is in it (LB-F57)
